{{About|the scientist|other people named David Peterson|David Peterson (disambiguation)}}
'''David L. Peterson''' (born 1954) is an Emeritus Senior Scientist (formerly research biologist) with the [[United States Forest Service]] and professor at the School of Environmental and Forest Sciences, at the [[University of Washington]]. He was also a co-founder and lead scientist for the Western Mountain Initiative,<ref>Western Mountain Initiative. {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20100527165205/http://westernmountains.org/people.php Principal Investigators]}}</ref> a consortium of researchers known world-wide for their work on the effects of climate change on mountain ecosystems.{{cn|date=July 2024}}

==Biography==

Peterson received a Ph.D. in 1980 from the [[University of Illinois]], and has   published over 200 scientific papers <ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.cfr.washington.edu/research.FME/pubs/dlp_pubs.htm | title=David L. Peterson Publications |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100618012214/http://www.cfr.washington.edu/research.FME/pubs/dlp_pubs.htm |archive-date=2010-06-18 }}</ref> in dendroclimatology, ozone air pollution, climate change and adaptation to global warming, and decision support systems for fire management.

He was invited to serve on the board of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] (IPCC).   He has also received  awards: from the International Union of Forestry Research Organizations (IUFRO),<ref>{{Cite web | title=IUFRO World Congress 2005 Special Award | url=https://www.iufro.org/fileadmin/material/publications/news-noticias/news05-awards-special.pdf}}</ref> the "Chief's Award", the highest honor within the US Forest Service, and honorary life membership in the Northwest Scientific Association <ref>[http://www.northwestscience.org/Default.aspx?pageId=937585 Northwest Scientific Association Honorary Life Members]</ref> for his leadership in research in the Pacific Northwest, USA.

Peterson is a lead investigator for forest ecosystems for the National Climate Assessment, and lead author for the first comprehensive guidebook <ref>{{Cite web | title=Responding to climate change in national forests: a guidebook for developing adaptation options | url=http://www.treesearch.fs.fed.us/pubs/39884 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628035218/http://www.treesearch.fs.fed.us/pubs/39884 | archive-date=2017-06-28 | last1=Peterson | first1=David L. | last2=Millar | first2=Connie I. | last3=Joyce | first3=Linda A. | last4=Furniss | first4=Michael J. | last5=Halofsky | first5=Jessica E. | last6=Neilson | first6=Ronald P. | last7=Morelli | first7=Toni Lyn | last8=Peterson | first8=David L. | last9=Millar | first9=Connie I. | last10=Joyce | first10=Linda A. | last11=Furniss | first11=Michael J. | last12=Halofsky | first12=Jessica E. | last13=Neilson | first13=Ronald P. | last14=Morelli | first14=Toni Lyn }}</ref> for adapting to climate change on U.S. forest lands.  He continues to lead [[climate change adaptation|adaptation to climate change]] on federal, state, tribal, and private lands.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://adaptationpartners.org/|title=Adaptation Partners|website=adaptationpartners.org}}</ref>

Peterson is lead or co-author of four books: Ecological Scale: Theory and Applications (1998),<ref>Ecological Scale: Theory and Applications {{ISBN|0-231-10502-9}}</ref> Human Ecology and Climate Change (1995),<ref>Human Ecology and Climate Change {{ISBN|1-56032-404-X}}</ref> Climate Change and United States Forests (2014),<ref>Climate Change and United States Forests {{ISBN|978-94-007-7515-2}}</ref> and Climate Change and Rocky Mountain Ecosystems (2018).<ref>Climate Change and Rocky Mountain Ecosystems {{ISBN|978-3-319-56928-4}}</ref>
